confidence_rationale: Filed supports at moderate confidence, and the moderation is deliberate: this is a formal precedent, not empirical evidence. VNS specifies exactly the escalate-on-stagnation, reset-on-improvement dynamic that MECH-527 asserts, which matters because that half of the claim has no biological support in this pull -- Karlsson gives the decay but not the escalation. Source quality is high for what it is (the canonical statement of a widely used metaheuristic). Confidence is capped at 0.70 because an optimization metaheuristic being effective on combinatorial problems is weak evidence that a brain does anything similar, and REE's biology-before-formal-definitions invariant means a formal match should inform naming and design rather than count as grounding.
failure_signatures: VNS supplies the escalation rule that the biological literature in this pull does not: on failure to improve, the search moves to a broader neighborhood (k <- k+1); on any improvement it collapses back to the narrowest (k <- 1). MECH-527's escalating breadth under continued stuckness with decay after resolution is therefore an already-formalised algorithm, not a novel structure.

The trigger in VNS is failure to improve after search at the current level -- not any measure of ambiguity or uncertainty among candidate solutions. This is an independent formal precedent for keying perturbation to non-resolution rather than to near-ties, matching MECH-527 and not MECH-440.

Because a well-known algorithm already has this shape, presenting the escalation/decay dynamic as a new mechanism would over-claim novelty. What is genuinely open in MECH-527 is whether a cognitive architecture implements it, not whether the control structure is a sensible one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Variable Neighborhood Search is a metaheuristic that explores a nested sequence of neighborhoods of increasing size around an incumbent solution. Its control structure is explicit: after shaking and local search within neighborhood k, an improvement causes the search to recentre on the new incumbent and reset to the narrowest neighborhood, while a failure to improve causes the search to move to the next, broader neighborhood. Systematic change of neighborhood is what allows the search to escape local optima that a fixed-neighborhood local search cannot.
mapping.ree_translation: Two uses for MECH-527, both about form rather than evidence. First, it supplies the escalation half of the claim as an already-specified rule, and it does so with the same trigger MECH-527 chose: failure to improve, not ambiguity. Second, and more consequential for the claim's disposition, it means the escalate-then-collapse dynamic has an established name. MECH-527 would be better positioned as the hypothesis that a VNS-shaped control structure is implemented above the action level in a cognitive architecture -- and that Karlsson-style network resets are its biological signature -- than as a newly coined mechanism. That framing is both more defensible and more citable, and it makes the claim's novel content explicit: not the control structure, but the assertion that a brain-like architecture uses one.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is the weakest kind of evidence in the pull and should be weighted accordingly. Combinatorial optimization over an explicit solution space with a well-defined objective and a computable improvement test is not what an embodied agent faces; 'failure to improve' is decidable in VNS and is exactly the quantity MECH-527 must estimate noisily from experience. Nothing here is evidence that any biological system implements VNS, and under the project's biology-before-formal-definitions invariant a formal analogue must not be allowed to stand in for biological grounding. I include it because MECH-527's escalation half would otherwise be entirely unsupported, and because a rename recommendation needs a concrete alternative to point at.
mapping.source_context: Combinatorial and global optimization; metaheuristic design, with the original four-page statement of the method.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high as the canonical reference for a widely adopted method. Mapping fidelity 0.55 and transfer risk 0.70 are both deliberately unflattering: this is an optimization algorithm, not a finding about any organism, and its structural match to the claim is a reason to align naming and design, not a reason to raise confidence that the mechanism is real.
